claim: Comparing metaheuristics based on an equal number of objective function evaluations is described as 'standard practice' in the metaheuristics/swarm-optimization literature, establishing budget-matched comparison as a field-wide norm rather than an ad hoc control this batch is only inferring.
stance_target: budget-matched comparison as an established methodological norm across black-box/metaheuristic optimization benchmarking, which the AAAI-27 draft's query-budget-matching correction instantiates but does not cite as belonging to a named tradition
scope_conditions: Metaheuristic and swarm-optimization algorithm benchmarking, IEEE CEC-competition context
quoted_support: "Comparing various metaheuristics based on an equal number of objective function evaluations has become standard practice."

claim: Raising the evaluation budget can significantly affect the final verdict of a metaheuristics comparison, i.e. which algorithm is judged best changes with the number of function evaluations allowed.
stance_target: deliverable (iii): budget level changing which optimizer wins is a documented phenomenon in a sibling optimization literature (metaheuristics/CEC competitions), not a novel isolated finding
scope_conditions: Swarm algorithms and IEEE CEC competition winners under varying evaluation budgets
quoted_support: "Even though the final impact varies based on current algorithm selection, it may significantly affect the final verdict of metaheuristics comparison."
